summary: arXiv:2610.24806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite breakthroughs in AI-driven molecular generation, existing discovery pipelines operate largely in silico, with wet-lab feedback reserved for validation rather than iterative improvement. title: Bypassing Current Biosecurity Screens with AI Designed Proteins and Closing the Gap with Edge-AI Functional Screening
summary: DNA synthesis machines are vital tools in medicine and research, but they can be misused to produce sequences which are transcribed and translated to produce toxic proteins. Synthesis providers may screen orders for dangerous sequences, but most screening software performs sequence-based alignment, which is vulnerable to AI redesign attacks. title: PHANES: an integrated resource of protein features for the human proteome
summary: Protein analysis and machine-learning workflows increasingly rely on large-scale numerical representations of proteins. While protein language models provide powerful embeddings, their limited interpretability and high computational cost hinder their use in many biological applications. We present PHANES, a human proteome database and web server providing a comprehensive, biologically interpretable set of features for 20335 proteins. summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) target evidence is distributed across biological, chemical, structural, regulatory, and trial-registry sources, complicating reproducible target evaluation and modeling. summary: Computational protein design workflows require the orchestration of multiple tools, data formats, and analysis steps that are often fragmented. title: IRE1α undergoes a dynamic filament assembly cycle governed by unfolded proteins and BiP.
summary: The endoplasmic reticulum is a major hub of protein synthesis, modification and trafficking that relies on the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) to balance its folding capacity. title: Heimdall SNAREs reveal an ancestral architecture of eukaryotic SNARE complexes
summary: SNARE proteins are central to eukaryotic cell biology, where they drive membrane fusion by assembling into four-helix bundles that bring opposing membranes into close proximity. Their ubiquitous role in intracellular membrane trafficking raises fundamental questions about their evolutionary origin and the emergence of eukaryotic cellular complexity. title: Dual-portal ligand transport in human cytochrome P450 17A1
summary: Human cytochrome P450 17A1 (CYP17A1) is the qualitative regulator of steroidogenesis, catalyzing both 17-hydroxylation and 17,20-lyase cleavage at a single active site, and is the target of the prostate cancer drug abiraterone. title: Network organization of protein binding-site landscapes across scales
summary: Studying protein binding sites helps explain ligand recognition and selectivity, informing drug development and repurposing. Here, we combine protein language model embeddings with network analysis to investigate how local recognition environments organize across scales. title: Proteome scale drug prioritization from AlphaFold 3 interaction confidence
summary: AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts protein ligand complexes, but the utility of its confidence scores for drug prioritization remains unclear. We benchmarked AF3 interaction scores against BANDOCK+, an experimentally informed approach, using approved drugs and human protein libraries. AF3 ipTM achieved similar aggregate disease ranking performance to BANDOCK+, with differences among individual indications. These results support the evaluation of AF3 interaction confidence as a source of information for proteome scale drug prioritization.

summary: Designing ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules with prescribed structures and functions is central to RNA engineering. summary: Molecular dynamics simulations are powerful tools for studying protein behavior, yet their accuracy remains limited by the approximations of molecular force fields and the difficulty of determining their parameters. Moreover, existing force fields are largely optimized for globular proteins and can perform poorly on structurally distinct systems. summary: Functional genomics in crops increasingly depends on integrating information from an extensive literature and heterogeneous multi-omics datasets. summary: MYC is one of the most frequently dysregulated oncogenic drivers across many cancers, yet direct therapeutic targeting has remained difficult because its function is mediated by disordered regions and transient protein-protein interactions. summary: Type II ABC importers rely on substrate-binding proteins (SBP) to capture nutrients and deliver them to membrane-embedded transporters, but how ATP binding and hydrolysis regulate their interactions remains poorly understood. summary: The Rho GTPase RhoJ is a key regulator of tumour angiogenesis and has been identified as a target for anti-angiogenic drug design. summary: RAB27A is a member of a highly conserved family of small GTPases that regulate intracellular vesicle trafficking.
